learned: The probe fires 15.6x more often than iFVG signals — 56% of triggers hit the swept-extreme stop before displacement/inversion fires. variant: sweep_bos Phase 1 -- OTE retrace bucket analysis (MNQ 5min, 5y excl 2022)
learned: OTE retrace depth is inversely correlated with BOS forward performance on NQ 5min: no-retrace bucket (WR 84.4%, PF 18.90) strictly dominates OTE bucket (WR 37.1%, PF 2.06). 56% of BOS events see price return through the sweep extreme (stop) within 20 bars -- the stop anchor is at the wrong level for BOS entries, same root cause as B33's probe rejection.

learned: Prior-day directional bias (close vs open) does not predict iFVG signal quality on NQ 5min — the gate reduces volume by 86% and worsens both PF (0.84 vs 1.00) and combine passes (4/61 vs 7/61). learned: ORB-reentry r=0.5 achieves higher sust (3.08x with B31 Phase A) than B21's r=0.75 (2.85x) but $/mo collapses to $246 vs $508 â€” far below the $300/mo useful threshold. The pipeline is throughput-constrained at r=0.5: only 13 funded accounts open over 5 years (vs 14 at r=0.75), earning $1,935/account (vs $3,131) with 126-day average durations. r=0.75 is confirmed as the Phase B optimum: it is the lowest risk level where per-account net is high enough for meaningful $/mo given pipeline supply constraints.

variant: FVG-midpoint stop placement (fvg_mid + fvg_mid_abs vs swing baseline)
learned: The FVG zone midpoint lies inside the normal gap-fill retracement path that price traverses during valid iFVG development. Placing a stop at the midpoint guarantees premature stop-outs on setups that would otherwise resolve in favor of the signal. Both fvg_mid and fvg_mid_abs lost on BOTH objectives vs the swing-stop baseline. Root cause is geometric: for iFVG entries, the stop must be placed OUTSIDE the FVG zone (at or beyond the distal edge). The swept-extreme stop is geometrically correct â€” it sits past the liquidity sweep that price must not revisit for the trade thesis to hold.

variant: ORB-reentry r=1.0 and r=1.25 Phase B sensitivity
learned: ORB-reentry's sust advantage over plain ORB (0.21x at r=0.75) reverses at r=1.0: reentry generates 41 funded busts (sust 0.83-0.90x) vs plain ORB's 27 busts (sust 1.37x) at the same r-multiple. The second-entry mechanism amplifies bust frequency faster than it improves per-account earnings at aggressive sizing. r=1.25 hits $523-545/mo but sust collapses to 0.71-0.77x. r=0.75 is confirmed as the Phase B risk optimum from both below (B32: r=0.5) and above (B38: r=1.0/r=1.25). The B31 winner ($508/mo, sust 2.85x) remains undefeated.

variant: iFVG-edge r=2.0 research baseline Phase A

At the research baseline (engine=ifvg, named sessions, no MNQ overrides), r=2.0 Phase A generates only 12 passes over 82 attempts â€” far fewer than r=1.25's 34/162 â€” producing $394/mo, sust 0.92x (worse than B21 on both metrics, stop rule triggered). The deployed config generates 25 more passes at the same r=2.0 risk level: the combined engine + all-day killzones produce more monthly trades, shifting the monthly P&L distribution toward passing rather than busting. variant: combined-engine Phase A r1.25 -> ORB-reentry r0.75
learned: The B40 combine-harness result (10/61 monthly passes, 2x better than ifvg-only) does NOT transfer to better funded pipeline throughput. The combine harness forces one attempt per calendar month; the funded pipeline model runs CONTINUOUS attempts. Combined engine's higher trade frequency (9.1/month vs 4.3/month for ifvg-only) damps per-attempt equity variance, meaning each attempt takes longer to resolve (12.7d vs 6.0d). Fewer total attempts = fewer total funded accounts (10 vs 34 over 5y). The higher per-attempt pass rate (24% vs 21%) is overwhelmed by 4x fewer total attempts. Lesson: combine-harness pass rate and funded-pipeline throughput are structurally decoupled â€” more trades per unit time slows the attempt cycle by dampening variance, not accelerating it.

variant: ORB signal window cutoff (orb_signal_window_mins=60 and =90)
learned: ORB signals after 10:30 ET (60 min post-open, n=84 over 5y) are structurally loss-making (PF 0.622-0.963). Cutting them with orb_signal_window_mins=60 removes 8% of signals while: (1) keeping all 10/61 combine passes, (2) improving combine PF 1.15->1.21 (+5.2%), (3) reducing Phase B busts from 25 to 22 (-12%), (4) improving two-phase sust 1.68x->1.91x (+14%). The deployed config (with partial_r=1.5) would see proportionally similar bust reduction. w=90 has same bust reduction but better $/acct ($1,932 vs $1,725) at cost of 1 combine pass. w=60 is the recommended value: cleaner (no pass degradation), mechanically sound (removes exactly the documented loss-making 10:30-11:30 ET segment).

learned: Per-hour PF analysis must be validated within the EXACT deployed config subset. The wk2-r4 per-hour analysis (ifvg_edge, all-sides, all-day) showed 11-13 ET at PF<1. In close-mode LongOnly all-day, the same hours are PROFITABLE: blocking them reduced combine passes 45->39 (-13%), combine PF 1.11->1.00, long net $25k->$5.8k over 61 months (51 fewer exits, avg $380/trade profit lost). Two infrastructure improvements shipped: CLI --set coercion fix for list[int] fields (regression test added) and --exclude-years flag for equity_export.py (holdout protocol compliance).

variant: ideation: iFVGÃ—ORB directional confluence, rank hybrid filter, breakout extension
learned: London iFVG and NY ORB provide independent directional confirmation of day structure. When both agree on direction, signals from both engines are dramatically higher quality: ORB same-direction PF=1.689 vs opp-direction PF=0.957; iFVG orb_same PF=1.375 vs orb_opp PF=0.757. Consistent in 5/5 years for ORB suppress-opp (+1.5-12.9% per year), 4/5 for iFVG suppress-opp (2021 exception PF=1.030, borderline). First cross-engine quality gate found that is both causal (iFVG fires London before ORB fires NY; ORB fires before post-ORB iFVG re-entries) and year-by-year consistent. Mechanism: multi-session order flow alignment -- when London and NY sessions agree on direction, structural conviction compounds; when they disagree, both signals fail. New backlog: B47 (confluence gate, GO-status Phase 2), B48 (rank hybrid filter), B49 (ORB breakout extension Phase 1).

variant: B42 Phase A + deployed Phase B w=0 vs w=60
learned: orb_signal_window_mins=60 does NOT improve deployed pipeline sustainability: both w=0 and w=60 Phase B produce identical bust counts (13) and sust (3.23x), but w=60 reduces per-account earnings by $591 (-19%), lowering $/mo from $549 to $456 (-17%). The B43 candidate finding (bust reduction at partial_r=0) does not transfer to the deployed partial_r=1.5 config because partial exits smooth the equity curve and prevent busts that the window cutoff would have otherwise blocked. Key confirmation: deployed partial_r=1.5 produces identical pipeline economics to research-parity partial_r=0 (B46 w=0 = B21 ref exactly), validating B25's finding that partial exits have negligible pipeline impact at ORB r=0.75.

variant: iFVG x ORB directional confluence gate (G1+G2) on combined engine, deployed params
learned: The iFVGxORB directional confluence gate (remove ORB when all prior same-day iFVG oppose it; remove post-ORB iFVG opposing ORB direction) hurts the combined engine: funded sust drops 0.79x to 0.50x (-37%) and combine pass rate drops 23.5% to 17.6% on the 2025-2026 test set. Despite removing 692 trades (-14%), 5y net P&L falls $24k ($95k to $71k). The Lesson-91 finding (ORB opp-direction PF=0.957) was valid in isolation but the gate over-filters: it also removes profitable ORB trades where the iFVG signal happened to oppose direction without predicting ORB failure. Secondary finding: the combined engine baseline itself has sust=0.79x vs the separate Phase A+B pipeline at 3.23x â€” running both engines on one account does NOT match the two-account pipeline performance.

variant: ifvg_max_short_rank=1 (rank-1 both sides + all longs) vs LO baseline
learned: Close-mode rank-1 iFVG shorts are loss-making (PF 0.84) in the deployed config despite being profitable in the research baseline (PF=1.127 with ifvg_edge). The entry mode fundamentally changes short signal quality: close-mode fires at the inversion bar close (zone_low for shorts), which is structurally weaker than the ifvg_edge retrace entry. The B48 hybrid adds 272 iFVG shorts at deeply negative expectancy, reducing both combine passes (11 vs 12) and PF (1.09 vs 1.21) vs the long-only baseline. The long-only filter is the correct deployed config for iFVG shorts in close-mode.
